EightPuzzle.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initializes an 8-puzzle solver instance by storing the caller-supplied starting board configuration and binding the canonical solved state as a fixed goal." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> initial_state </REF>: list "A 3x3 nested list representing the starting tile configuration of the 8-puzzle, supplied entirely by the caller with no validation performed"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Bind self.initial_state to the value of the initial_state parameter as provided by the caller, without copying, validating, or transforming it RESULT self.initial_state]
            [COMMAND Bind self.goal_state to the literal 3x3 nested list [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 0]], where 0 at position [2][2] represents the blank tile in the solved 8-puzzle configuration RESULT self.goal_state]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
EightPuzzle.find_blank:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Scans a 3×3 grid in row-major order and returns the (row, column) coordinates of the first cell whose value is exactly 0, or implicitly None if no such cell exists." find_blank]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "The instance of the class containing this method"
        <REF> state </REF>: list[list[int]] "A 3×3 two-dimensional list representing the puzzle board, where 0 denotes an empty cell"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: tuple[int, int] | None "A (row, column) tuple identifying the first empty cell found, or None if the board contains no cell equal to 0"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Begin iterating i over the integer range [0, 1, 2], representing row indices of the 3×3 board RESULT outer_loop_i]
            [COMMAND For the current value of i, begin iterating j over the integer range [0, 1, 2], representing column indices; cells are visited in row-major order: (0,0), (0,1), (0,2), (1,0), …, (2,2) RESULT inner_loop_j]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop over i and the inner loop over j, evaluate whether state[i][j] is strictly equal to the integer 0 (falsy values such as None or False do not satisfy this condition) RESULT cell_is_blank]
            [COMMAND If cell_is_blank is True, immediately return the tuple (i, j), exiting both loops and the method without scanning any remaining cells RESULT early_return_coordinates]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: All 9 cells have been visited and none equals 0 — both loops complete without triggering the early return]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Fall through to the end of the method body, implicitly returning None to the caller RESULT implicit_none_return]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
EightPuzzle.move:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Applies a sliding-puzzle move by locating the blank tile in the given state, creating a shallow copy of the board, and swapping the blank with its neighbor in the specified direction before returning the modified copy." move]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> state </REF>: list[list[any]] "2D list representing the current puzzle board, where one cell contains the blank tile"
        <REF> direction </REF>: str "Cardinal direction of the move; one of 'up', 'down', 'left', or 'right'"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> new_state </REF>: list[list[any]] "Shallow copy of the board with the blank tile swapped one step in the specified direction; original state is left unchanged"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call self.find_blank(state) and unpack the returned two-value sequence into row index i and column index j, identifying the current position of the blank tile RESULT i, j]
            [COMMAND Create new_state as a shallow copy of state by building a new outer list where each inner list is an independent slice copy of the corresponding row in state RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND Evaluate the string value of direction and execute exactly one of the four swap branches: if 'up', atomically swap new_state[i][j] with new_state[i-1][j]; if 'down', atomically swap new_state[i][j] with new_state[i+1][j]; if 'left', atomically swap new_state[i][j] with new_state[i][j-1]; if 'right', atomically swap new_state[i][j] with new_state[i][j+1]; if direction matches none of these four values, no swap is performed and new_state is returned unmodified RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND Return new_state as the result of the method RESULT new_state]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: direction does not match any of 'up', 'down', 'left', or 'right' — the if/elif chain falls through with no else branch]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip all swap operations and return new_state unchanged as a plain shallow copy of state RESULT new_state]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
EightPuzzle.get_possible_moves:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Determines the list of valid directional moves for the blank tile in a 3x3 sliding puzzle grid by checking boundary conditions on the blank tile's row and column coordinates." get_possible_moves]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "The puzzle solver instance, providing access to find_blank"
        <REF> state </REF>: any "The current puzzle board state passed to find_blank to locate the blank tile"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> moves </REF>: list "Ordered list of valid move direction strings; each element is one of 'up', 'down', 'left', 'right'"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize moves as an empty list to accumulate valid direction strings RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND Call self.find_blank with state and unpack the returned 2-tuple into row index i and column index j representing the blank tile's position in the 3x3 grid RESULT i, j]
            [COMMAND If i is strictly greater than 0 (blank is not on the top row), append the string 'up' to moves RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND If i is strictly less than 2 (blank is not on the bottom row, using inclusive upper bound 2 for a 3-row grid), append the string 'down' to moves RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND If j is strictly greater than 0 (blank is not on the leftmost column), append the string 'left' to moves RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND If j is strictly less than 2 (blank is not on the rightmost column, using inclusive upper bound 2 for a 3-column grid), append the string 'right' to moves RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND Return moves as the final list of valid directions RESULT moves]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
EightPuzzle.solve:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Performs a breadth-first search from the initial state to the goal state, returning the sequence of moves that constitutes the shortest path, or null if no path exists." solve]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance providing initial_state, goal_state, get_possible_moves(state), and move(state, move) attributes and methods"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> path </REF>: list or null "Ordered list of moves leading from initial_state to goal_state, or null if no solution exists"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize open_list as a list containing a single tuple of (self.initial_state, empty_path_list), where self.initial_state is read once at call time and the empty list represents zero move history RESULT open_list]
            [COMMAND Initialize closed_list as an empty list to track all states that have already been expanded RESULT closed_list]
            [COMMAND While open_list is non-empty (truthy check), dequeue the front element using pop(0) to enforce FIFO / BFS ordering, unpacking it into current_state and path RESULT current_state, path]
            [COMMAND Append current_state to closed_list immediately after dequeuing, marking it as visited before any expansion RESULT closed_list]
            [COMMAND Check whether current_state equals self.goal_state using exact equality; if true, return path immediately as an early exit from the entire method without further expansion RESULT path]
            [COMMAND Within the while loop, iterate over every move yielded by self.get_possible_moves(current_state) to enumerate successor actions from the current state RESULT move]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over moves, compute new_state by calling self.move(current_state, move) to apply each candidate move to the current state RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, check whether new_state is not in closed_list (linear membership scan, O(n)); if the state has not been visited, append the tuple (new_state, path + [move]) to the back of open_list, extending the recorded path by the current move RESULT open_list]
            [COMMAND If the while loop exhausts open_list without triggering the goal-state early return, fall through and return null to signal that no solution was found RESULT null]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: open_list becomes empty before any state equals self.goal_state, meaning the entire reachable state space has been explored without finding the goal]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Exit the while loop naturally and return null RESULT null]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: new_state is already present in closed_list after a move is applied]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip appending (new_state, path + [move]) to open_list entirely, preventing re-expansion of already-visited states and avoiding cycles RESULT open_list unchanged]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
